# Soups and Broths

## Bone Broth

Bone broth is made by simmering animal bones for an extended period to extract collagen,
gelatin, minerals, and marrow. Roast the bones first at 400 degrees for 45 minutes to develop
deep brown color and roasted flavor through the Maillard reaction. Combine with cold water,
apple cider vinegar to help extract minerals, onion, carrot, celery, and aromatics.
Simmer on the lowest possible heat for 12 to 24 hours without boiling, which would cloud the broth.

## Chicken Stock

Simmer a whole chicken or chicken parts with mirepoix (onion, celery, carrot) and a bouquet
garni of thyme, bay leaves, and parsley stems. Cook at a bare simmer for three to four hours.
A properly made chicken stock gels when refrigerated, indicating sufficient gelatin extraction.

## Vegetable Broth

Roast or sweat onion, leek, carrot, celery, garlic, tomato, and mushrooms before simmering.
Mushrooms add umami depth. Kombu seaweed added during the last hour boosts glutamates
without overpowering the vegetable flavors. Simmer for 45 minutes; longer cooking makes
vegetable broth bitter.

## French Onion Soup

Caramelize thinly sliced onions in butter over very low heat for 45 to 60 minutes until deeply
golden and sweet. Deglaze with dry white wine and cognac. Add beef stock and simmer for 30 minutes.
Ladle into oven-safe crocks, top with baguette slices and gruyere cheese, and broil until bubbly.

## Miso Soup

Dashi, made from kombu and katsuobushi (dried tuna flakes), forms the base of miso soup.
Dissolve miso paste directly into the warm dashi without boiling, which destroys the beneficial
enzymes. Add silken tofu and sliced green onions.
